Here’s @Tesla’s update post/article from last year to review!


Tesla (@Tesla)

x.com/i/article/191069540703…



— https://nitter.net/Tesla/status/1910848021065052629#m

Tesla released their Spring Update this week last year. 🌸☀️

It included Adaptive Headlights in North America, Alternative Trip Plans, Keep Accessory On, a redesigned Dashcam UI, and many other features.

What would you like to see in this year’s update?

Here is the post we are referencing regarding the camera issue and the upsate being pulled from pending installs.


Teslascope (@teslascope)

We have received two unconfirmed reports from vehicle owners that the update 2026.8.6 was pulled due to delays with loading the rear camera and receiving the error “Camera Temporary Unavailable”.

The scope of this bug is not known, but is not impacting all Tesla vehicles.



— https://nitter.net/teslascope/status/2042787811791900715#m

This software update 2026.8.6.1, now going wide, resolves the rear camera delay/blackout issue we reported on previously, which impacted many, but not all Tesla vehicles on 2026.8.6.

We expect vehicles on the prior version will be prioritized initially, as seen in our data.


Teslascope (@teslascope)

We noticed a new Tesla software update 2026.8.6.1 on Model X Plaid (2022) in Texas, United States. View the rollout of this update here: teslascope.com/software/2026…




— https://nitter.net/teslascope/status/2043177584276508961#m

This appears to be an older update that was not previously detected on our platform, but was released in limited quantities starting on March 18th.

The update includes Full Self-Driving V14.1.4, so it is an older version of FSD.
We noticed a new Tesla software update 2026.4.5 on a Tesla vehicle (2023). View the rollout of this update here: teslascope.com/software/2026…

teslascope.com/software/2026…
We noticed a new Tesla software update 2026.8.6.1 on Model X Plaid (2022) in Texas, United States. View the rollout of this update here: teslascope.com/software/2026…

The software update 2026.3.6 has been released in the Netherlands, and contains Full Self-Driving (Supervised) V14.2.2.5.

The release notes do not mention V14.2.2.5, although has been confirmed both in-vehicle and within the official @Tesla mobile app.

We had observed a number of reports on this issue since the update was first released over a week ago, but typically resolved itself after a reboot.

As this directly impacts safety, we believe this is the cause of the update being pulled, and may be re-released with fixes.

We have received two unconfirmed reports from vehicle owners that the update 2026.8.6 was pulled due to delays with loading the rear camera and receiving the error “Camera Temporary Unavailable”.

The scope of this bug is not known, but is not impacting all Tesla vehicles.


Teslascope (@teslascope)

We’ve observed a majority of Tesla vehicles with 2026.8.6 pending (whether awaiting install or download) have had the update pulled from their vehicles worldwide. This also impacted our own vehicle.

No official insight into the decision at this time can be provided.

Full Self-Driving (Supervised) is OFFICIALLY approved in the Netherlands.

It will begin rolling out to customers shortly.



— https://nitter.net/teslascope/status/2042710416837742726#m

RDW has stated that Full Self-Driving (Supervised) has been extensively tested and makes a positive contribution to road safety. They reiterated that it is safer than other systems.

Expansion to all member states of the European Union is now possible.

rdw.nl/nieuws/2026/toelichti…

De toekomst van mobiliteit is aangebroken

FSD Supervised has been approved in the Netherlands 🇳🇱 & will begin rolling out in the country shortly! 

Trained on billions of kilometers of real-world driving data, it can drive you almost anywhere under your supervision – from residential roads to city streets & highways

No other vehicle can do this. 

We're excited to bring FSD Supervised to more European countries soon
